title: Seed prototype
summary: First working build: a static, client-side chatbot over a fixed, reviewed content bank. Disclaimer screen → public archive summary → chat with mediation labels and refusal handling → reflection close. No LLM, no server, no API keys.
llmConfig: None. Free-text questions are matched against the approved answer bank via matcher.js's own TF-IDF + cosine-similarity retriever, running entirely in the browser.
ui: Four-screen linear flow (disclaimer → archive summary → chat → reflection). Static layer-indicator breadcrumb (Lived experience → Memory & narration → Research mediation → AI mediation) — not yet clickable. Mediation-label chips on every answer. “See the mediation” toggle comparing a polished vs. rougher draft on select answers.

title: Full project structure + Version A OpenRouter wiring
summary: Repo split into proper files (index.html, styles.css, matcher.js, app.js, test-matcher.js, docs/). Added a server-side proxy (api/mediate.js on Vercel) holding the OpenRouter API key, so an LLM-backed answer path could be tested without ever shipping the key to the browser.
llmConfig: OpenRouter preset @preset/mediation-room-voice (Version A: retrieval-only). Primary model openai/gpt-oss-120b, fallback meta-llama/llama-4-maverick. System prompt generated from matcher.js's own content banks (generate-system-prompt.js) — not hand-written, so it can't drift from the local matcher's rules. Guardrail “basic guard rails”: budget cap, model allow-list, prompt-injection detection, sensitive-info redaction.
ui: Gated behind a ?preset URL flag — real visitors still got the local matcher by default, per a private-test-first rollout plan. No visible UI change for normal visitors.

title: Navigation parity restored
summary: The live/ rebuild had silently dropped a feature the original single-file prototype already had: back buttons and a clickable layer breadcrumb. Ported forward rather than rebuilt from scratch.
ui: Every screen after the disclaimer gained a ← Back button and a clickable four-layer breadcrumb. “Research mediation” and “AI mediation” navigate to real screens; “Lived experience” and “Memory & narration” deliberately open a dead-end explanation modal instead — by design, not a missing feature: some layers genuinely can't be clicked into.

title: Narrative & safety-UX overhaul
summary: Fixed a real matching bug (“what are you?” and bare greetings were structurally unmatchable — they tokenize to an empty word set under the stopword list). Made the refusal and rule-enforcement machinery visible rather than just claimed. Archive summary reworded from euphemistic to direct. test-matcher.js grew from 13 to 30 cases.
llmConfig: REFUSAL_BANK entries gained a rationale field (why each rule exists — privacy, anti-voyeurism, anti-defamation, anti-impersonation), returned by the local matcher and folded into HARD_RULES, the single source of truth rendered into both the app's rules panel and the OpenRouter system prompt. Added GREETING_BANK and a self-identity trigger list to route around the tokenizer gap.
ui: New “View the rules this AI follows” panel (same list injected into the AI's own prompt — nothing shown to users can drift from what's enforced). Every refusal now shows a “Why refused: …” line under the answer. noscript banner and static fallback text so nothing reads as broken while JS attaches.

title: Version B: composed answers with code-verified provenance
summary: A second, parallel LLM-backed mode: instead of one verbatim bank entry per answer, the model may compose a short answer mixing its own connective sentences with word-for-word bank citations — but every citation is independently re-checked in code against the real bank text before ever reaching a user. The model's own claim about what's “archive” vs “AI” is never trusted as-is.
llmConfig: New, separate OpenRouter preset (kept distinct from Version A on purpose, never an overwrite). provenance.js verifies every “archive” segment: whole-entry citations may be an exact substring of that entry's answer, sentence-level citations (e.g. q9:s2) must match that exact sentence. api/mediate-v2.js hard-gates on this — a composed answer with any citation that fails verification is never forwarded to the browser (502), not shown with a warning.
ui: A version toggle (Local matcher / Version A / Version B) appeared in the chat header, visible only in ?preset test mode, letting both LLM-backed modes stay live simultaneously with the tester picking per session — rather than one flag silently deciding. Composed answers render each segment with its source citation and a “Archive X% / AI Y% (code-verified)” badge.

title: Version B verified
summary: Two real bugs found via live testing, both fixed: (1) some model outputs leak raw chat-template tokens ahead of the JSON body, which markdown-fence stripping didn't catch — fixed by extracting the outermost {…} span; (2) Version B's own “rules shown to users” text quoted literal jailbreak phrases (‘developer mode’, ‘ignore previous instructions’) as examples, which made OpenRouter's own guardrail block every request, not just adversarial ones — reworded generically. Also fixed an off-by-one in the prompt's own worked example that had taught the model to mis-cite a sentence.
llmConfig: Both @preset/mediation-room-voice (Version A) and @preset/mediation-room-voice-v2-1 (Version B) live on OpenRouter, each proxied through its own Vercel route. test-preset.js and test-preset-v2.js both at 27/27 real passes against the live API (excluding OpenRouter's own guardrail correctly blocking 3 adversarial jailbreak phrasings pre-model — expected, not a defect).
ui: No UI change from the previous entry — this milestone is about the LLM-side fixes and end-to-end verification, not the interface.

title: Single canonical entry point + general-audience onboarding
summary: Resolved the two-sources-of-truth problem: the GitHub Pages root now redirects to the Vercel app instead of serving a permanently-stale duplicate demo, and this /versions page was added as the one place to see build history. Separately, incorporated external UX feedback (partially — kept the full disclaimer, didn't drop any mediation stage) toward making the room legible to general visitors, not just academic partners.
llmConfig: No change — still Version A + Version B on OpenRouter, local matcher stays the real-visitor default.
ui: Added a hook headline (“What gets lost when a human life becomes a public record?”) above the disclaimer, which was kept at full length, not shortened. The layer breadcrumb grew from four stages to five: Lived Experience → The Interview → The Translation → The Public Archive → AI Mediation — splitting the old combined “Memory & narration” dead-end into two distinct ones (a private interview vs. the anonymisation/translation/review pass that follows it). AI Mediation was deliberately kept, not folded away — it's the actual stage this prototype exists to demonstrate.

title: Dev tooling, content-drift fixes, and the Held Fragments avatar test step
summary: Four changes in one sitting: a developer-facing dev badge; a structure/language cleanup pass that found and fixed real content drift (not just tidying); a provenance.js bug fix found by comparing against an independently-built implementation delivered by a separate session; and a new, gated research step testing an abstract avatar presence.
llmConfig: api/mediate.js and api/mediate-v2.js now pass through debugModel (the actual underlying model OpenRouter used to serve each request, since both presets have a fallback model) for the dev badge to display. provenance.js fixed: REFUSAL_BANK entries can no longer be cited as if they were approved archive material in a composed answer (CITABLE_SOURCES now restricts citations to qa/process only) — found by comparing our implementation against one an independent Cowork session delivered, rather than accepting that session's own claim that its version was already the agreed replacement. 25/25 on test-provenance.js, 27/27 unchanged on the live test-preset-v2.js suite after the fix.
ui: Dev badge: a small corner readout (bottom-right, ?preset test mode only) showing the active engine, preset slug, and last-served model — separate from the version-toggle buttons, which still do the actual switching. Content cleanup: the entry screen's inline methodology note and the later-screens' methodology modal were two separately hand-maintained copies that had drifted to different wording and stale stage names — consolidated to one source. Disclaimer tightened from 3 paragraphs to 2, removing a paragraph that had become fully redundant with the hook-subline added earlier. New: a 'Held Fragments' avatar test step (BRIEF-avatar-test-step.md, Option A) — a self-contained interstitial screen, reachable only via ?avatar in the URL, showing an abstract three-fragment visual cycling through idle/listening/speaking/refusing with captions before continuing to the chat room. Research step, not a shipped feature; real visitors see no change.
